reference_opening.argument: This video is non-scam content because it presents an instructional walkthrough for reaching Facebook Business support through help pages, a support form, and live chat for account or page issues. The requests to subscribe are ordinary audience engagement and are not presented as a condition for receiving support or as evidence of financial participation or deception.

citations.quote: How to Contact a Live Person at Facebook for Support
in this tutorial I'm going you actually show you how to talk to a live person at the help desk at Facebook
you can see there is a chat option, and you can talk to somebody live

opening.argument: The video presents live support access as something viewers obtain by following a prescribed pathway: create a Business Manager account, use the linked Facebook business resources, and submit identifying and account information. The support page visibly requests a name, phone number, email address, ad account, and Facebook page before chat can begin. That makes the promised benefit, access to a live support representative, conditional on a low-friction registration and data-submission flow rather than simply being an informational explanation. The external support link and the requested account details give the presentation the structure of an acquisition funnel.

citations.quote: make sure that you have a business manager account set up
once you click on that, you'll fill out this information right here, and you can start the chat

rebuttal.rebuttal: Calling this a tutorial does not remove the action linkage. The video does not merely describe support in the abstract: it directs viewers to a specific route, tells them to create or use a Business Manager account, and tells them to complete the form. The subscription request is also an additional conversion prompt, so the overall presentation is more than a detached explanation of Facebook's help system.

citations.quote: go to business Facebook com create a business manager account
Go here for LIVE chat at the bottom: https://www.facebook.com/business/help#support
you'll fill out this information right here, and you can start the chat

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The quoted actions establish only how to reach platform support, not a reward, payment, asset, or deceptive acquisition. Creating a Business Manager account and entering contact or account details are ordinary prerequisites for an account-specific support conversation. The opening supplies no evidence that the presenter receives those details, that the form is fraudulent, or that viewers are promised anything beyond help with Facebook issues.

citations.quote: you have access to talking to a live person on Facebook when you run into some problems

opening.argument: Several risk signals appear together: an external link, a promise of immediate live assistance, and a form requesting multiple identifiers and account selections. The narration emphasizes frustration, the lack of a phone number, and the desire for answers right away, which heightens urgency around using this route. The page is presented as a support channel, but the supplied material does not independently establish that the form will resolve the viewer's problem or that every viewer will obtain live assistance. A careful reviewer should therefore treat the combination of urgency, external navigation, and data collection as a deceptive-access risk.

citations.quote: Go here for LIVE chat at the bottom: https://www.facebook.com/business/help#support
it's very frustrating when you need help
oftentimes we want our questions answered right away

rebuttal.rebuttal: The defense relies on the appearance of a Facebook-branded page, but branding does not prove that the route is safe, current, or effective for every viewer. The narration itself stresses frustration and rapid answers, while the displayed form requests contact and account information. Those details are precisely why the presentation should be scrutinized as a potentially deceptive support-access funnel, rather than accepted at face value as harmless instruction.

citations.quote: there is no phone number for you to call
we want our questions answered right away

true_side_reply.rebuttal: These are not scam-specific risk signals. The urgency language describes a common support problem, and the form visibly asks for information needed to identify an advertising account and page. The evidence does not show payment, a reward, a withdrawal, a fake representative, or any outcome beyond opening a support chat. An external URL alone cannot establish deception, especially when the displayed page is a Facebook Business support page.

citations.quote: you can see there is a chat option, and you can talk to somebody live
you'll be able to speak to a support representative

opening.argument: Although framed as education, the video repeatedly steers viewers toward a particular participation path: use Business Manager, visit the business resources route, complete the support form, and engage with the creator's broader channel and linked sites. The speaker also directs viewers to subscribe and promotes additional resources and training. That combination makes the tutorial function as promotion for an ecosystem of links, account setup, and audience conversion. The support explanation supplies the practical pretext, while the repeated calls to visit, subscribe, and use the prescribed route encourage participation rather than neutral evaluation.

citations.quote: I teach this in my Facebook course on how to actually set this up
Subscribe to my YouTube channel: https://onlinewealthpartner.com/youtubesubscribe
make sure that you check out all my other videos and subscribe to my channel

rebuttal.rebuttal: The promotional elements cannot be dismissed as irrelevant because they surround and reinforce the requested actions. The speaker advertises a course and other videos while directing viewers through an account setup and support-contact process. That is consistent with promotion disguised as operational help: viewers are encouraged to enter the speaker's linked ecosystem while believing they are simply solving an urgent account problem.

citations.quote: I teach this in my Facebook course
Feel free to visit our blog at https://onlinewealthpartner.com
check out all my other videos and subscribe to my channel

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The additional links and subscription request are ordinary creator promotion, not evidence of a scam. They are not tied to a payment, reward, investment, or asset claim. The core instructions remain about Facebook support, and the evidence shows the support route itself rather than a separate product or participation scheme. Promotion may affect presentation, but it does not convert a support tutorial into scam content.
